calls.head: Vejmelka gets another crack at the Oilers
calls.body: Vejmelka has been shaky against the Oilers since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Vejmelka starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .899 than to his .858 against the Oilers.

calls.happened: Karel Vejmelka stopped 12 of 17 shots (.706), against his usual .899 and his .858 against this team before tonight.

calls.title: Vejmelka struggled against the Oilers again
calls.plain: Vejmelka’s night looked more like his record against the Oilers than his usual. Three seasons of evidence say it’s still a coincidence.
calls.said: Vejmelka’s rough record against the Oilers was a coincidence, and he’d look like himself

calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Mammoth
calls.body: The Mammoth roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six. Utah is the league’s best for depth, and Edmonton is one of the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Mammoth.

surprises.body: Vejmelka allowed 5 goals on 17 shots, worth 2.0 expected goals: 3.0 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 35 starts.

story.head: Five points for McDavid as the Oilers beat the Mammoth
paras: Zach Hyman was back in the lineup after missing six games. Connor McDavid opened the scoring for the Oilers just 40 seconds into the game, and Hyman made it 2-0 on the power play midway through the first. Mathieu Joseph scored his first goal for Edmonton 32 seconds later to make it 3-0. Trent Frederic and Jack McBain dropped the gloves late in the first. Kasperi Kapanen and Leon Draisaitl scored just under three minutes apart midway through the second to stretch the lead to 5-0. Utah pulled Karel Vejmelka after five goals and turned to Sebastian Cossa for the rest of the second. John Marino and Mikhail Sergachev scored a minute and a half apart early in the third to cut Edmonton’s lead to 5-2. McDavid scored again a little over four minutes later to make it 6-2 for the Oil. He added three assists for a five-point night.
The chances were closer than the score. Tristan Jarry made 26 saves for the Oilers. The Oilers moved to 6-1-1, second in the Pacific, while the Mammoth dropped to 6-3-0, still first in the Central.
